correctness.rationale: All maximal shortest paths are 3-cell Ls because the rook graph has diameter two, and every edge extends to an L. The explicit 2x2,2x3,3x3 and 4x4 witnesses plus independent three-row/four-row strip decompositions prove sharpness for any dimensions. For two rows, uniqueness of the pivot-column, pivot-row and rowwise wing injections gives the all-packing sum. The uncovered-cell L criterion is an if-and-only-if; disjoint-hole counting yields the maximal polynomial, and the exceptional 2-hole full column is counted separately. Algebraic simplifications give the three maximum multiplicities. An independent graph-distance program checked every coefficient for n=2..7 and 225 rectangle witnesses.

value.rationale: Natural sharpness question for the same rook graph family used to introduce geodesic packing. For every nontrivial rectangle the general order upper bound is attained constructively, and for the thin factor the complete packing and inclusion-maximal packing polynomials are determined, as well as a nontrivial interval of maximal ranks and all residue-class factorial maximum counts. These classify a full infinite family of packing configurations, not a numerical sample or routine change of variable.
